{"id": "dc0eed84-b2f1-4e21-a015-efd98da6070d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The minimum is four controls. Together they mean no prompt change can reach production without passing a measured check.

**1. Prompts live in version control and deploy only through a pipeline**
- Keep the system prompt in a repo, not in a console or a runtime setting that people can edit.
- Require a pull request with a reviewer. Branch protection should block direct pushes.
- Give only the pipeline role permission to deploy the prompt. Without this, the other controls can be bypassed.

**2. A fixed evaluation set that runs on every prompt change**
- Build a golden dataset from real traffic. Include the known failure cases and the edge cases. Start with a few dozen to a few hundred examples and grow it over time.
- Run the evaluation automatically in CI whenever the prompt changes. A job someone has to remember to run doesn't count. On Bedrock this can be an automated model evaluation job, or a RAG evaluation job if you use a knowledge base.
- Score the candidate and the current production prompt on the same dataset and compare them.

**3. A promotion gate that blocks on regression**
- The pipeline fails if the candidate scores worse than production beyond a tolerance you set.
- AWS publishes no universal threshold for this, so you choose it per workload.
- Judge scores can be noisy. Run enough examples that a difference you see is larger than the run-to-run variance. Otherwise you'll get false alarms or miss real regressions.
- Include safety and refusal checks, and add some human review. Automated judges have blind spots, so a single score shouldn't be the only thing you trust.

**4. Production monitoring to catch what the offline set missed**
- Watch the finish-reason distribution, specifically a shift from normal completion toward `max_tokens`. That means answers are being truncated, and it often shows up hours or days before users complain. It isn't a CloudWatch metric. You can only get it from Bedrock invocation logs, so you need invocation logging on and a metric filter on the stop reason.
- Watch output token counts and error rates.
- Keep rollback to the previous prompt version as a one-step operation. Prefer a gradual rollout or canary over switching all traffic at once.

**Priority if you can only do one thing:** lock down who can deploy (control 1), then add the automated gate (controls 2 and 3). Monitoring limits the damage from a regression. It doesn't prevent one.

I can't see your CI/CD pipelines from AWS APIs, so I can't confirm whether evaluation is wired into deployment. I can check your account, read-only, for Bedrock evaluation jobs. That would show whether any have ever run, how recently, and whether invocation logging is enabled. Tell me which region and account to look at if you want that.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
